decisions.addendum: The audits are planned by the quality manager under a written procedure and take place at least once a year.
decisions.reason: Regular scheduled internal audits, with a fixed minimum frequency and a written planning procedure.

decisions.addendum: Risk-based criteria pick the most critical activities to audit, including, where relevant, how actions from the previous audit were implemented.
decisions.reason: Audit procedure defines scope; adds risk-based selection and follow-up of earlier actions.

decisions.addendum: Auditors are trained and independent of the activity they audit.
decisions.reason: Independent audits by competent staff; adds independence from the audited activity.

decisions.addendum: Audit conclusions are also discussed at management review and communicated to staff.
decisions.reason: Reporting audit results to management; adds management review and staff communication.
Corrections and corrective actions after audits are implemented promptly.
Monitoring the effectiveness of corrective actions, here only for those arising from audits.

decisions.addendum: Records also show how the audit programme has been carried out.
decisions.reason: Keeping audit records; adds evidence of programme implementation.

decisions.item_text: The laboratory is headed by a director (or equivalent) who holds a university degree in a suitable discipline, has supervisory experience in pharmaceutical analysis gained in a quality control laboratory, the regulatory sector or industry, and carries full responsibility for all analytical, organisational, administrative and educational operations.
decisions.reason: No listed requirement covers the qualifications and role of the laboratory head.

decisions.item_text: The laboratory head makes sure that laboratory staff have the competence and qualifications their functions need and that their grades match their responsibilities.
decisions.reason: No listed requirement covers staff competence and grading in the laboratory.

decisions.item_text: The laboratory head makes sure that the adequacy of the existing staff training procedures is reviewed periodically.
decisions.reason: No listed requirement covers periodic review of training procedures.

decisions.item_text: The laboratory head makes sure that technical management is adequately supervised.
decisions.reason: No listed requirement covers supervision of technical management.

decisions.item_text: The laboratory head makes sure that certificates of analysis, analytical test reports and other important reports and protocols are approved.
decisions.reason: No listed requirement covers approval of laboratory reports and certificates.

decisions.item_text: The laboratory head is preferably supported by one or more technical managers or senior analysts with extensive experience of pharmaceutical analysis in quality control, who are designated as responsible for analytical operations and for directly managing and supervising the analysts and technicians.
decisions.reason: No listed requirement covers technical managers supporting the laboratory head.

decisions.item_text: The laboratory has a quality manager with the responsibility and authority to put the quality management system and quality control activities in place and to make sure they are complied with.
decisions.reason: No listed requirement covers a laboratory quality manager.

decisions.item_text: Depending on the size of the laboratory, the quality manager is kept independent of routine analytical work.
decisions.reason: No listed requirement covers the quality manager's independence from routine analysis.

decisions.addendum: The quality manager organises the audits, preferably with a staff member from another section, to a schedule approved at management review.
decisions.reason: Scheduled internal audits; adds the organiser, cross-section participation and schedule approval at management review.

decisions.item_text: The quality manager, with technical managers' support where needed, makes sure that staff who operate specific equipment, instruments or other devices are competent for those tasks.
decisions.reason: No listed requirement covers competence of equipment operators.

decisions.item_text: The quality manager makes sure that staff who carry out tests, calibrations, validations or verifications are competent for those tasks.
decisions.reason: No listed requirement covers competence of staff doing tests, calibrations and validations.

decisions.item_text: The quality manager makes sure that regular in-service training is arranged to update and extend the skills of analysts and technicians.
decisions.reason: No listed requirement covers in-service training of analysts and technicians.

decisions.item_text: The quality manager makes sure that the laboratory regularly takes part in suitable proficiency testing schemes and, where possible and applicable, in collaborative studies.
decisions.reason: No listed requirement covers proficiency testing.

decisions.item_text: The quality manager makes sure that substances under poison, narcotic, psychotropic or radioactive controls are safely kept and controlled: stored locked away, and handled and used only in designated areas, supervised by an authorised person.
decisions.reason: No listed requirement covers custody of controlled substances.

decisions.item_text: The laboratory has qualified analysts, normally holding a degree in pharmacy, analytical chemistry or another relevant subject, with the knowledge, skills and ability to perform the tasks given to them.
decisions.reason: No listed requirement covers analyst qualifications.

decisions.item_text: Suitably qualified and experienced analysts are available to act as laboratory supervisors, with a thorough understanding of the management system, including reviewing, interpreting and reporting results, keeping an internal chain of custody, and applying corrective and preventive actions for analytical problems.
decisions.reason: No listed requirement covers availability of laboratory supervisors.

decisions.item_text: Technicians hold a diploma in their subject from a technical or vocational school, or have the hands-on experience their assigned activities need.
decisions.reason: No listed requirement covers technician qualifications.

decisions.item_text: The laboratory has a suitable training schedule for its staff, in particular for those who meet its technical and managerial needs.
decisions.reason: No listed requirement covers a laboratory training schedule.

decisions.item_text: Inputs to the training plan may be taken from internal audits, management reviews, risk and opportunity assessments or other available sources.
decisions.reason: No listed requirement covers inputs to the training plan.

decisions.item_text: When training is completed successfully, the evaluation results are recorded and made available, and the competency matrix or master list is updated.
decisions.reason: No listed requirement covers recording training results in a competency matrix.

decisions.item_text: The quality management system makes sure that sufficient resources, such as equipment, staff and materials, are available.
decisions.reason: No listed requirement covers provision of sufficient resources.
Applying the relevant GMP and related guidelines, here only for excipients.
Responsibilities defined in job descriptions, here only for managerial roles.
Operations are described in written procedures.
Arrangements for correct materials, here only for containers and labels.
Necessary controls are in place, without the demand that all risks are identified.

decisions.item_text: Calibrations, verifications or validations are carried out wherever they are necessary.
decisions.reason: No listed requirement states the general need for calibration, verification and validation.

decisions.item_text: Each excipient is processed and checked correctly, following the defined procedures and specifications.
decisions.reason: No listed requirement covers correct processing and checking against procedures and specifications.

decisions.item_text: Every deviation, suspected product defect, out-of-specification result and other nonconformance or incident is reported, investigated and documented.
decisions.reason: Listed deviation requirements cover only critical deviations or investigation depth, not reporting and recording of all nonconformances.

decisions.addendum: The most likely root causes are identified.
decisions.reason: Suitable depth of root cause analysis; adds identifying the most likely causes.
Changes evaluated and approved beforehand, without the regulatory notification element.
Post-implementation evaluation of changes for quality objectives and unintended harm.

decisions.addendum: Where appropriate, the effectiveness of these actions is checked.
decisions.reason: Identifying and taking CAPA; adds effectiveness checks.
Processes for managing outsourced activities.

decisions.item_text: No batch of a pharmaceutical excipient is released or supplied until the quality unit has released it, having assured itself that the batch was produced and controlled in line with the product specifications, applicable GMP guidance and any other rules on production, control and release.
decisions.reason: Listed release requirements cover active substances and medicinal products, not excipients.
A system for handling complaints, returns and recalls.
Only requires a self-inspection system, without regular scheduled audits.
Only requires a product quality review system, without naming the quality unit.

decisions.item_text: Management makes sure the quality management system meets its intended objectives and measures how it is run and how it performs, in areas including self-inspections, inspections, quality and supplier audits; complaints, returns and recalls; changes and deviations; rejected batches; quality control, out-of-specification and out-of-trend results; equipment maintenance; qualification and validation; corrective and preventive actions; and risk management.
decisions.reason: No listed requirement covers management measuring quality system performance.

decisions.addendum: Written programmes exist for periodic self-inspections, quality audits and supplier audits.
decisions.reason: Written audit procedures; adds programmes covering quality and supplier audits.
Self-inspections carried out routinely under a programme.
